rationale: Round 0 compiled and passed cleanly with no ICE, so this candidate escalates obfuscation strength for bisort's profile: a tiny (1697 text bytes, 14 functions) recursive benchmark whose hot paths (Bimerge, RandTree, bitonic recursion) tolerate modest overhead. FLA and BCF get the highest security/diversity weights to break control-flow recoverability of the recursive merge-sort and tree-building loops; SUB stays high since arithmetic substitution is cheap and the program is mult-heavy; IBR and ICALL are raised to interleave blocks and opaque indirect calls, hampering static call-graph recovery on a small binary where cross-referencing is easy. RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights are held mid-range rather than maximal because the reference binary is already small and overhead budget is acceptable-but-not-unlimited; CorrectnessRisk weights stay at or below 0.4 since round 0 confirmed the toolchain handles these passes on this program, but flattening recursion still warrants the most caution. All seven passes remain enabled to maximize combined diversity on such a small attack surface.
